Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: sealed-subnet / tenant egress attestation request

Mina,

Thanks for taking this — Everline is collecting formal attestation material for our vendor risk review. Two items we need answered in sufficient detail for our auditors: 1) a deployment-level diagram showing sealed subnets (control plane vs data plane), egress enforcement points, and any sidecar/proxy boundaries; and 2) a short threat-surface summary that explains how an attacker would (or would not) be able to exfiltrate tenant data across the inference fabric (high-level attack steps + mitigations).

Can you provide diagrams and an evidence bundle we can reference in our assessment by Dec 15? Also let us know if you prefer a short sync to walk through the diagram.

Appreciate it — Claire
Claire Dawson
Senior Vendor Risk Manager
Everline Financial

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: sealed-subnet / tenant egress attestation request

Claire —

Thanks, we can do that. Attaching the current sealed-subnet diagram (v2) and an egress evidence packet draft. High-level notes up-front: we separate the control plane (management/orchestration) from tenant inference pods via network microsegmentation and host-side enforcement; tenant workloads run in sealed subnets with strict outbound allowlists enforced by egress proxies and firewall rules. Our threat summary below covers plausible attack paths and the controls that materially reduce risk.

We can run a 30-minute review call on Dec 10 or Dec 14 — which works better for your team?

Attachments: sealed-subnet-diagram-v2.png (diagram), egress-policy-evidence.pdf (evidence packet)

Regards,

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: diagram review + threat matrix updates

Mina / Ben —

Quick internal note before we send the final bundle to Everline: I updated the diagram to call out the following explicitly — control-plane API endpoints are in a separate management VPC with no direct routing from tenant subnets; sidecars terminate mTLS to egress proxies and do not accept inbound connections; KV cache is per-tenant with ACLs enforced at the runtime. I also added an appendix row showing fallback routing behavior (model-variant fallback to a smaller pool) and why that does not expose data paths.

Ben, can you paste the short attack-step bullets into the attack-surface-matrix.csv and confirm the CVSS-like severity column? I want to keep the external-facing summary to one page and push the matrix internally.

Thanks — Kim

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: INTERNAL: diagram review + threat matrix updates

Kim / Mina / Irene —

Uploaded the attack-surface-matrix.csv to the shared folder and added three rows:
- Lateral compromise of control plane (vector: stolen control-plane creds) — likelihood: low, impact: high — mitigations: HSM-backed keys for control-plane, multifactor for operators, per-request auth tokens
- KV cache leakage (vector: shared memory telemetry misconfiguration) — likelihood: medium-low, impact: medium — mitigations: per-tenant KV namespaces, runtime enforced ACLs, token-scoped access
- Egress proxy misconfiguration (vector: wildcard allowlist) — likelihood: low, impact: high — mitigations: config linting, deploy-time policy validation, automated policy tests

Irene, can you confirm the egress proxy telemetry logs are retained for 90 days in our evidence PDF? I referenced 90 days in the packet but want to be sure.

Ben

Subject: Sealed Subnet Attestation & Attack Surface Summary (Everline RFI)

Claire —

Please find attached the attestation bundle for Everline's RFI: sealed-subnet-diagram-v2.png (annotated topology), egress-policy-evidence.pdf (retention and telemetry appendix), and attack-surface-matrix.csv (detailed step mapping and mitigations). Key takeaways in brief:
- Control plane and data plane are segregated at VPC and routing layers; there is no direct route between tenant subnets and our control-plane management network.
- Tenant inference workloads run in sealed subnets with egress proxies enforcing allowlists; proxies use mTLS to upstream destinations and deny unknown hosts by default.
- Per-tenant KV namespaces and runtime ACLs reduce risk of cross-tenant leakage; cache eviction and key rotation cadence described in the packet.
- Telemetry required for audit (egress evaluations, TLS metadata) is retained for 90 days; archived evidence exports available on request.

If helpful, we can walk through the diagram and the attack-surface CSV in a 30-minute call. I'm available Fri Dec 17 10:00-11:00 or Mon Dec 20 13:00-14:00 PT.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
